result.briefing:
**Briefing for Quality & Sourcing: CASE-07F53D, SYNTH-RiverLoafer / Quality (confidence High)**

- **Signal:** 16 of 20 style returns in 90 days are Quality returns (80%, against a 4.6% baseline). They run across 9 stores, online and mail, both banners and sizes 37–42, in the weeks of 01-05 to 01-26. The latest is #6027 on 01-30. #940 reports "sole separating". Nothing in the data names a lot or supplier, and no one has inspected a unit yet.
- **Done automatically:**
  - I opened the case, recorded the findings and notified Quality & Sourcing.
  - I waived restocking fees of CA$52.76 on returns #179, #3636, #3925 and #6677, which is within the CA$500 limit. Future returns of this style and category are fee-free while the case is open. No customer return is restricted.
- **Waiting for approval:**
  - Stock hold on the DC and stores (APR-FD8449): Quality and Merchandising.
  - Supplier quality claim (APR-BC1EC8): drafted, not sent. Quality & Sourcing must approve it before it goes out.
  - Proactive outreach to recent buyers on opted-in channels, offering a free return or replacement (APR-3A73D0): Customer Care and Privacy.
- **Needed from Quality & Sourcing:** inspect the returned units (#940 first) and trace receiving dates and lot/PO numbers for recent stock. This would test whether a single lot is the cause. It would also firm up the supplier claim.
- **Verification on 2026-02-21:** I will re-run the screen once the pending approvals are resolved. The check needs at least 5 recent style returns and snapshot coverage through that date, otherwise it is inconclusive. If Quality is still at WATCH or above, the case reopens and the hypotheses are revised. If it is back to normal, the case can close, but that doesn't prove the actions caused the drop.

result.briefing:
**Briefing for Merchandising: CASE-07C0B3, SYNTH-TrailRunner, "Fit: too big" (confidence High)**

- **Finding:** All 20 returns in the last 28 days are "too big". That is 74% of 27 returns over 90 days, against an 11.8% company baseline. All 20 are in sizes 41, 42 and 43, and none are in sizes 37–40. The pattern covers both banners, online, mail and store channels, and 4 stores. I ruled out a quality defect, an expectation gap, transit damage and normal noise. Local store handling and a mislabelled lot stay inconclusive, because there are no lot or supplier fields to test them.
- **Done automatically:** I opened the case, recorded the findings and notified Merchandising (ACT-01B838). I did not waive restocking fees, because 0 of 20 customers were charged one and fit is not an ALDO-fault class. No customer returns are restricted.
- **Waiting for approval:** Merchandising needs to decide APR-C0B743. It is a product-page note for sizes 41–43: "Sizes 41-43 run large… we recommend trying half a size down. Free returns and exchanges are available if the fit isn't right."
- **Not actioned:** The playbook only allows stock hold, supplier claim and proactive outreach for confirmed quality cases. Because there were no such returns in Nov–Dec, I would not assume the design simply runs large. A new lot, last or size-label change is plausible, but I can't prove it. Please ask Sourcing and Quality to check for a lot, last or size-spec change around the turn of the year and to measure stock in those sizes.
- **Data gap:** No returns of any kind appear for 15 Dec to 4 Jan. Please confirm whether that is missing data, because it affects when the problem started.
- **Verification:** A check is scheduled for 21 Feb 2026. It will confirm that the signal has fallen below WATCH and that there are at least 5 recent returns. It will also check whether the pending approval has been resolved. If the signal is still at WATCH or higher, the case reopens.

result.briefing:
**Briefing for Logistics (CASE-19406B, SYNTH-CoastalBoot, Damaged in transit)**

- **Finding:** 12 of 17 returns in the last 90 days are transit damage (70.6% against a 2.4% company share). All 12 came in the last three weeks (2, 5 and 5 per week from the week of Jan 12), and none came earlier. Confidence is Medium, and the likely cause is damage in the shipping chain (carrier or packaging).
- **Done automatically:** I opened the case, recorded the findings and notified Logistics. I did not copy E-commerce Ops (DC), because the notify tool only takes one team. Logistics may want to loop them in.
- **Fees waived:** The tool refunded restocking fees on 5 returns (#1851, #2396, #2543, #3699, #5699), CA$59.00 in total. That is within the CA$500 limit. Future returns of this style and category are fee-free while the case is open. No customer returns were restricted or delayed.
- **Waiting for approval:** Nothing. Stock hold, supplier claim and proactive outreach need High confidence and a Quality-class cause, so I did not propose them. I also did not propose a fit-guidance update, because fit and expectation causes were ruled out.
- **Asked of Logistics and DC:** Please pull carrier, ship date, DC and box type for the 12 returns, and check for recent carrier, packaging or DC changes. That would separate carrier damage from packing damage. I'd also suggest Quality visually inspect returned units to test the lot-defect explanation. I couldn't send that request through a tool, so someone needs to raise it with them.
- **Verification due 2026-02-21:** I'll re-run the screen. If the signal is still at WATCH or SIGNAL, the case reopens and the hypotheses get revised. A normal signal can close it.
